title: Only one mythology tells how the world ends
cover:
4 mythologies.
Only one tells the end of the world

scenes.text: Four mythologies. Only one tells how the world ends.
The Greeks have no apocalypse. Hesiod only foretells the end of a race of men: the gods and the world go on.
The Egyptian texts read here have none either: the dead are promised millions of millions of years.
Ovid, the Roman poet, leaves a single sentence: one day, a fire will destroy the universe.
But the Norse poem Voluspa tells it stanza by stanza. The wolf breaks its fetters. Heimdall blows the horn.
Odin falls to the wolf. Thor kills the serpent, walks nine paces… and dies.
The sun turns black, the earth sinks into the sea, and the stars fall from the sky.
And the part people forget: the earth rises again from the waves, green. And Baldr comes back.
One detail: Hesiod and the Voluspa share a sign of the end. Brother against brother.
Which text says so? The Voluspa, in the Poetic Edda.
Save it, and send it to anyone who thinks every mythology has its apocalypse.
